Executive Summary

This report covers 332 accounts across 11 DN Realty Corp properties with a combined placement value of $2,117,931.54 and a current outstanding balance of $2,107,870.57. Total collections to date are $8,294.00 (0.4% liquidation rate).

Southwest Recovery Services has executed 28,637 collection activities against this portfolio since the first placement on October 27, 2025, averaging 86 activities per account. Activity breakdown: 12,987 phone calls, 10,750 collection emails, 1,402 letters, 271 validation notices, 761 skip-trace actions, and 116 credit bureau pulls.

Crystal at Riverdale is the largest location (118 accounts, $668,316 balance, 11,016 activities). Birch Creek and Crystal at Riverdale are the only locations that have generated payments to date ($8,294.00 combined).

The portfolio is early-stage — the majority of accounts (254) carry "New Business" status, indicating they are still within the initial collection campaign cycle.

Understanding Account Statuses

Each account carries a status reflecting its position in the recovery process. Some statuses mean direct collection activity has paused for a legal or compliance reason. A paused status does not mean the debt is forgiven, the account is closed, or that Southwest Recovery Services has stopped working. On property-management accounts, credit bureau and Experian RentBureau reporting continues on qualifying accounts even when direct contact stops — the unpaid balance follows the tenant to every future lease application.

New Business   254 accounts | $1,541,420

What it means: Active initial collection campaign — validation notices, dialer campaigns, email series, skip-trace, and credit bureau reporting where applicable.

Active 10 accts | $52,180    Follow Up 13 accts | $124,202

What it means: Contact made or attempted; collector is actively pursuing the debtor. "Follow Up" means a prior lead is being followed — these are closest to producing a payment.

Cease and Desist 16 accounts | $120,986

What it means: Direct collection communication (calls, letters, emails) has stopped. This is a legally required pause, not a write-off.

Why this protects you: Under FDCPA § 805(c) and Reg F § 1006.6(c), a debt collector must honor a cease-communication request. Continuing contact exposes both SWRS and the client to statutory damages and attorney fees.

What has NOT changed:

• The debt is still valid and owed
• The account remains open and on file
• Credit bureau and RentBureau reporting continues — the balance surfaces on every future tenant-screening report
• Co-debtors and guarantors without their own cease flag can still be worked
• The client retains all independent legal remedies
Client Remove 16 accounts | $100,394

What it means: These accounts were closed by SWRS after collection efforts were exhausted without the documentation needed to continue compliantly. In nearly every case: SWRS made initial contact attempts, but no supporting documents — signed leases, itemized ledgers, or move-out statements — were available at placement or provided upon request.

Why they were closed: Without a signed lease or itemized ledger, SWRS cannot substantiate the balance if disputed (FDCPA § 1692g), cannot verify fee authorization (FDCPA § 1692f), and faces accuracy exposure on credit reporting (FCRA § 1681s-2). Several were also flagged "Litigious Debtor" during skip-trace.

These accounts can be reopened. Provide the signed lease and itemized ledger, and SWRS will reactivate the account and resume full collection including credit bureau and RentBureau reporting.

Bankruptcy 5 accounts | $33,444

What it means: Automatic stay (11 U.S.C. § 362) prohibits all collection activity. SWRS monitors the case; collection resumes if dismissed or debt not discharged.

Deceased 8 accounts | $41,004

What it means: Debtor confirmed deceased. The debt is not extinguished — it becomes a claim against the estate. Co-debtors and guarantors remain individually liable.

Dispute 2 accounts | $10,037

What it means: Debtor formally disputed. Collection pauses until validated (FDCPA § 809(b)). Providing the signed lease and ledger accelerates resumption.

Skip Trace 3 accounts | $43,895

What it means: Debtor cannot be located. Skip-trace tools (LexisNexis, Accurint) are actively working to find current contact info. If you have updated contact info for these individuals, please share it with SWRS.

Paid/Settled 2 accounts | $2,500

Payment or settlement received. Target outcome.

Questions? Contact Southwest Recovery Services for a detailed timeline on any specific account.

Documentation & Compliance Advisory

Why This Portfolio's Recovery Rate Is Below Benchmark

The current liquidation rate (0.4%) is significantly below the NAA benchmark for property-management debt (15–20%). The primary driver is missing placement documentation.

SWRS makes an initial collection attempt on every account regardless of documentation status. This portfolio has received 28,637 collection activities across 332 accounts. However, when a debtor disputes or initial outreach doesn't produce payment, federal law requires validation capability before continuing.

FDCPA § 1692g: Disputes kill the file without verification documents.

Reg F § 1006.34: Compliant itemization requires the underlying ledger.

FDCPA § 1692e/§ 1692f: Fees must be authorized by the (missing) agreement.

FCRA § 1681s-2: Furnishing unsubstantiated balances = accuracy exposure.

What Documentation Unlocks
Without Documents
• Initial campaign only
• Cannot survive dispute
• No credit bureau / RentBureau reporting
• No litigation
• 4-year SOL (GA open account)
• Expected recovery: 4–12%
With Documents
• Full multi-channel campaign
• Can validate after dispute
• Credit bureau + RentBureau reporting
• Litigation available
• 6-year SOL (GA written contract)
• Expected recovery: 15–20%
Action Requested: Provide Supporting Documentation
• Signed lease + addenda/guaranty
• Itemized ledger / rent roll with dates
• Final account statement / SODA
• Move-in/move-out inspection + photos + invoices
• Notice to vacate / lease termination
• Dispossessory filing and judgment (if applicable)

Upload via portal.swrecovery.com or call (214) 387-8068.

Non-Working Accounts — Recovery Status & Credit Bureau Position

Property management collections do not follow a traditional "write-down" model. Unpaid balances are reported to Equifax, Experian, and Experian RentBureau — the database feeding tenant-screening reports. A reported balance follows the tenant to every future housing application. 51 accounts ($353,023) carry non-working statuses, but the majority continue to work passively through credit bureau and RentBureau reporting.

CBR / RentBureau Active — 18 accounts, $131,022.57

Direct contact paused — credit bureau and RentBureau reporting continues. The unpaid balance surfaces on tenant-screening reports, creating pressure when the tenant applies for their next lease.

Methodology & Data Notes

Data Sources: ADS Manager Complete Activity Report (28,637 activity entries) and Account Summary by Manager export (332 accounts), both pulled August 24, 2026.

Activity Period: October 27, 2025 through August 24, 2026.

Activity Classification: Each note entry classified into one category (Letters, Emails, Calls, Skip Trace, CBR, Validation, SMS, Other) based on keyword matching.

Financial Figures: Original Debt and Balance from ADS Account Summary. Payments reflect the Sum of Payments field (absolute value).

Regulatory Basis: All collection activity conducted in compliance with the FDCPA, Regulation F (12 CFR 1006), and the FCRA. Georgia state collection requirements apply.

Confidentiality: This report contains debtor PII and is intended solely for the authorized recipient.
